Bakhmut Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bakhmut, Ukraine

Demolished. NOTE: the source page's address, coordinates, and city fields for this record were found to actually belong to Cerová, Slovakia - a completely unrelated location - while the narrative text is genuinely about Bakhmut, Ukraine. The coordinates above are Bakhmut's actual town-center location, corrected from that error. Bakhmut (known as Artemivsk from 1924-2016) likely saw Jewish settlement begin in the early 19th century; by 1897, Jews made up 17% (3,259) of the population, supporting a synagogue, prayer house, beit midrash, three Jewish schools, and a Talmud Torah by the late 19th century, despite a 1905 pogrom. Population reached 5,299 (9%) by 1939. Roughly three-quarters of Bakhmut's Jews evacuated before German forces arrived in October 1941; the approximately 1,200 who remained were confined to a ghetto in November 1941 and murdered at a deserted alabaster quarry in February 1942. The community was re-established postwar, with renewed activity in the 1980s-90s; the 2001 census recorded 224 Jews in the city. This cemetery, founded in the late 19th century, was demolished in the 1960s, its grounds absorbed into the municipal cemetery. Per local testimony, some Jewish burials have continued informally among the Orthodox Christian graves at the site since then. (Note: Bakhmut has been the site of intense fighting during the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war since 2022-2023, which may have further affected the site; this record does not reflect any post-2022 changes.)
